section_summary.extract_value: This section details the testing of measurement invariance for Body Appreciation Scale-2 (BAS-2) scores across sex (women and men) and ethnicity (Malays and Chinese) within a full subsample of 781 participants. It reports that configural and metric invariance were found for both sex and ethnicity, but partial scalar invariance was achieved after relaxing constraints on specific items. An ANOVA revealed a significant main effect of Ethnicity on BAS-2 scores, with Malay participants showing higher body appreciation than Chinese participants, but no significant Sex x Ethnicity interaction or main effect of Sex.
section_summary.evidence_source: The entire section '3.3. Sex and ethnic invariance' and the note 'N = 781'.

Asset Caption.extract_value: Fig. 1. Path diagram and estimates for the one-dimensional model of Body Appreciation Scale-2 scores. The large oval is the latent construct, with the rectangles representing measured variables, and the small circles with numbers representing the residual variables (variances). The path factor loadings are standardised with significance levels were determined by critical ratios (all p < .001).
